title: Dreaming usually happens in REM sleep, when the eyes twitch and the muscles go limp
summary: NHLBI says dreaming usually happens during REM sleep, when the eyes twitch, brain activity looks like waking, and the muscles normally go limp.
body: NHLBI's stages page says sleep alternates between rapid eye movement, called REM, and non-REM. In REM, the eyes twitch and the brain is active. Measured brain activity in REM is similar to waking. Dreaming usually happens in this phase. Muscles normally become limp, which keeps a person from acting out dreams. Sleep studies sort the phases with sensors for eye movement and brain activity. This is a description of a typical night in that US text, not a claim that every dream was checked.

sources.title: How Sleep Works: Sleep Phases and Stages
